raw_response:
I farm only 4.1 mu, and I am 73, so I would keep things simple, steady, and low-risk. I already know wheat-maize rotation well, and with well irrigation I would stay with the same system instead of trying anything complicated. For wheat, I would use improved seed, put enough fertilizer to keep the stand strong, irrigate a few key times, and manage weeds and disease with limited but timely spraying. For summer maize, I would use hybrid seed because it gives me more stable production, especially on small land. I would put most fertilizer at sowing and early growth, irrigate when the crop most needs water, and spray only when pressure is real. I would use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing and works well enough on my small field. My goal is not chasing the highest possible yield. I would aim for stable yield, manageable labor, and lower chance of loss.
